📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a new laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

Recent findings suggest that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you plan to buy a new laptop while there are holiday savings.

In a recent development, apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple users saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

According to recent reports, apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

It has been revealed that how much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple people paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” noted Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

In a recent development, if you blueprint to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — presently MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

Recent findings suggest that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple owners mentioned their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

In a recent development, digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple users seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

Industry observers note that take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple users may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

Industry observers note that battery life is a massive deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook users saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

Comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo consumers say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test demonstrates that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Sources indicate that apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its users either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

“Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” stated Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook consumers have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

Industry observers note that and MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple owners reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their problems. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

Sources indicate that our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

It has been revealed that “Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” said Goldman.

Lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it notes encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

When it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple owners reported poor performance.

Here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without issues or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

In a recent development, on the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple users rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

Apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple consumers planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

Usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

According to recent reports, asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.

If you’re planning to spend that amount on a upcoming laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus customers say they’re extremely satisfied.

Asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. For example, the Zenbook A14 has a thin, lightweight design that’s rigid, with long battery life and an OLED display with strong contrast and color performance. This Copilot Plus PC sells for $1,600 (but retailers like Best Buy regularly have it on sale for less). Comparatively, these premium features from other brands could cost more or sacrifice crucial must-have features for the price.

Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.

Over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. Yet, 44% of Acer customers say their laptop has exceptional value, while 50% say the value is fair — bringing a total positive cost-to-value score of over 94%. Acer also has an overall satisfaction score of 92.6% — the highest of non-Apple laptop brands.

If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. It has a massive 16-inch screen but is still lightweight (3.5 pounds). And it has good battery life (over 21 hours on CNET’s battery drain test). There are a few other pluses, like the 1440p web camera that may be good for video conferencing and a sizable touchpad. All of those features and more add up to $700, which could make it a good computer for work or casual browsing. If you’re looking to spend slightly less, its predecessor, the Aspire 14 AI, is originally $639, but you may be able to score deals on both models during holiday sales.

It has been revealed that even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Here are a few non-Apple laptop brands that are runner-ups to CNET’s People’s Picks winners that you shouldn’t count out of your laptop search.

Lenovo is best known for packing a powerful laptop into a compact design with tablet functionality, like its Yoga line, and its durable ThinkPad business models. But CNET readers with Lenovo laptops say the brand’s battery life stands out most compared with other non-MacBook laptops.

Survey findings show that 16% of Lenovo owners say their laptops can run for 8 hours or more. And 10.5% say their laptop battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours, while 6% say their Lenovo laptops can withstand at least 10 hours before needing a charge. That’s more than what readers say about other non-Apple brands. The Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition lasts 25 hours and 45 minutes — making it one of the best laptop batteries CNET experts have tested.

Sources indicate that goldman said Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.

Recent findings suggest that if your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a newly introduced laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners said they haven’t had any hardware issues with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.

It has been revealed that beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.

If you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. And the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 is a business laptop with Lenovo’s well-known X1 Carbon exterior and new Space Frame design, which Elliott states makes it easier to repair or replace parts if needed.

Sources indicate that many Lenovo laptop users are loyal to the brand, which speaks to the overall positive satisfaction rating of 83%. If Lenovo owners were in the market for a newly introduced laptop, nearly three in four (73.2%) say they would buy another Lenovo laptop. Breaking down the percentage, 33.6% say they would buy the same model again. Meanwhile, 39.6% would buy a different model but stick to Lenovo.

Here’s why that might be. Lenovo offers a plethora of options to choose from based on your needs — while still evolving its laptops. For instance, the Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 has an open M.2 slot for a second storage drive and an OLED screen for crisp, colorful images — making it perfect for gaming. Its Yoga two-in-ones let you seamlessly switch between a tablet and traditional laptop, while Lenovo’s ThinkPad and ThinkBook business laptops offer everything from ultralight 2-pound bodies to expanding rollable screens. And its new designs don’t sacrifice the must-have needs like long battery life, durability and chip efficiency that lend to strong performance.

In a recent development, asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating  — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It’s super thin and lightweight, but it’s still sturdy thanks to its Ceralumnium body. Plus, it has supreme 24-hour battery life, 1TB of storage and an OLED display — all for $1,200. While that’s more expensive than some laptops, it’s what’s included in that price that makes it worthwhile compared with other non-Apple laptop brands.

Asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. That’s followed by 40.4% of Asus laptop owners who say it has very good task performance. When it comes to tasks, 37% primarily use their Asus laptops for work, while 5% use theirs for gaming.

Asus is well known for having lightweight laptops with all-day-and-night battery life and stunning display quality. Asus laptops like the Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 have a good port selection, which could be good for gaming, work or simply connecting different devices without the need for additional adapters. And the Asus Zenbook S 14 has a strong neural processing unit that contributes to its high-speed AI performance.

Asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. One common thread we noticed in Asus laptops is their OLED screens, which deliver high-resolution video and graphics. Asus laptops also combine stunning display quality with excellent performance and at surprisingly low prices for all of their features.

For example, the Asus Zenbook 14 isn’t the highest-quality OLED we’ve seen, but it still produces clear text and graphics on a 14-inch screen, along with exceptional black levels, Elliott stated. That’s still better than LCDs that many other non-MacBooks have, and could be the reason Asus owners rate it so highly in this category.

Dell wins our readers over as a top choice for high-end laptops. One-third (33.3%) of Dell owners spent over $1,500, and of that percentage, 15.2% spent over $2,000.

Industry observers note that dell’s premium laptops largely cater to business and gaming with their standout features and performance. The Alienware 16X Aurora is Dell’s midrange gaming laptop with user-replaceable RAM, a bright display and strong performance for $2,280. But if you want more gaming features, Dell has the Alienware 16 Area-51, which has even better gaming performance, upgradable RAM and three SSD slots for $2,530. And if you’re looking for a non-Mac alternative that comes close to MacBook quality and performance, the higher-end Dell XPS 14 is the one to choose. It has the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 graphics and 1TB of storage for $1,950.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella unveiled several fresh models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the firm.
  • Also: Microsoft says its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • Industry observers note that MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella unveiled several fresh models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the firm. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

Industry observers note that MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft noted it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the manufacturer has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the latest coding model the firm unveiled at Ignite.

Sources indicate that the company also released its newly introduced image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

Breaking: Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
  • A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

Sources indicate that apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

Recent findings suggest that back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

In a recent development, an Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

Apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and users. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple users flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

For many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

In discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community people to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others stated the site grew less helpful over the years.

Recent findings suggest that CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he remarked.

In a recent development, just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

It has been revealed that the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push customers away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

In a recent development, reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual consumers to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

In a recent development, apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The manufacturer may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum customers on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

Whatever the reason, the circle of Apple consumers helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar intends.

Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

According to recent reports, palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

Industry observers note that after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. Recent findings suggest that in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

Sources indicate that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Industry observers note that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

Recent findings suggest that but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
  • The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
  • Sources indicate that on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The latest program expands on the firm’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which launched in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole upcoming influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

Sources indicate that on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

First off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

As any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

According to recent reports, according to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

In a recent development, live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

Uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

It has been revealed that salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Industry observers note that brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a fresh brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Recent findings suggest that shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

Industry observers note that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

It has been revealed that agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent consumers using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

Sources indicate that the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

Recent findings suggest that today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

Latest Update: 11 Steps I Use for Quick Smart Home Prep for Guests and Holiday Visitors

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over.
  • If you have holiday or event looks involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices.
  • Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over. Since I test home security and multiple smart devices, I tend to have a lot. But they don’t have to be a distraction when you have visitors staying over. On the contrary, smart tech can usually help out.

If you have holiday or event looks involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices. These changes save me headaches and time, while impressing guests. You may even decide to enable some features year-round.

Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.

Doorbell chimes are just the start of your smart guest experience.

According to recent reports, video doorbells often come with a feature in settings to switch to seasonal themes, including a variety of holiday sounds for the end of the year. Vivint is particularly good at this, equipping its video doorbell with options for many different holiday songs. Google Nest doorbells and Eufy doorbells also have holiday options.

Smart lighting is easy to set up for certain times of day, dimming and brightening as necessary.

According to recent reports, cameras and guests don’t play well together. Help everyone feel safe by pulling down the shutters on your indoor cameras, nanny cams and smart displays (or disabling them through settings, etc.). Let everyone know their privacy is secured while staying over. Video doorbells and outdoor cams are fine to leave functioning, especially if you want to keep an eye on kids going crazy in your backyard.

Today’s smart lights include options to turn on at certain times of day or at sunrise, and at a specific brightness (and even color temperature). Some even allow you to gradually increase the brightness over an hour or so. Use these settings to set a simulated sunrise in key spots of the house to encourage guests to rise and shine at the right times. It’s especially handy if everyone needs to be up in the morning for a special activity — but make sure to provide coffee too.

Aqara’s app distills a whole lot of smart lock options into a highly digestible product card.

A smart lock allows for all kinds of tricks, like remote operation and auto-locking if it’s left unlocked. Those work great when you have guests over, but if you want to add even more options, many locks allow you to create temporary passes — including through common apps like Apple Home — and send them to your guest’s phones. That way they can come and go on their own schedules, and the door stays locked when no one is using it.

Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors, too.

In a recent development, keeping the thermostat triggering temperatures a bit low in winter is a great way to save energy, but not always the sign of a good host. Consider heading into your thermostat app and bumping up temperatures a few degrees, especially at night and the middle of the day, so everyone stays comfortable. The latest models can even sense humidity, which can be crucial if guests are sensitive to very dry or very wet air.

ADT’s new hub has a few extra tricks.

According to recent reports, home security system schedules usually call for arming the system during the day after everyone has left the house. That doesn’t work so well over the holidays, especially if you have guests over. Instead of disabling individual sensors, we suggest setting your home security system to disarm during the day.

Sources indicate that you can still get notable alerts from devices like leak detectors or package-recognizing video doorbells with the system disarmed. And you can leave the night mode armed (which usually lets people move around but monitors doors and windows closely).

A guest Wi-Fi network is an excellent add-on if you have multiple people coming to visit. It lets you set a separate network and easy-to-remember password for all guest devices, keeping your home network safer and letting you prioritize key home devices. Plus, you can keep reusing it whenever people come over in the future. We’ve got a full guide on how to set a guest network up, but it’s usually very easy with app settings.

Prep your smart speakers for guests to avoid any problems.

Sources indicate that smart home speakers like an Echo or the newly introduced Apple HomeView are excellent devices for playing holiday music for a whole house. But there’s a small problem: With a lot of extra guest devices on your Wi-Fi, music streaming may not be reliable. You can solve this problem by downloading a playlist to a device like a phone or tablet and playing it on the smart speaker via Bluetooth. Many common apps like Spotify let you do this, especially if you have a subscription.

Voice assistants are handy and fun, but they can be a distraction when others are around, especially if kids start getting creative in their commands. You could turn voice assistants off entirely, but we like the option to limit what they can do.

For example, Alexa has a Voice ID section in its settings that allows you to limit skills and third-party services from working with any voice except the profiles you create and add for you and direct family members. Google Assistant has a very similar option with its Voice Match settings, which limits device controls to only certain voices.

It’s also a good idea to set up a voice code to confirm any purchases made over voice assistants, so people can’t buy something with just a command.

A wireless charger nearly anyone can use.

It has been revealed that with the ubiquitous Qi charging standard, wireless chargers can work with nearly any phone. Make things easier for your guests by setting out a wireless charger or two for them to use without managing a tangle of power adapters. Bonus points if you offer chargers that have multiple charging pads, sparing your outlets even more.

If you have a little extra time, most home security systems can connect to compatible smart lighting and let you create routines to make them more useful. Specifically, we’ve had great results creating night mode routines for security sensors that turn on nearby smart bulbs at low brightness settings when motion is detected.

This way, if someone gets up in the middle of the night, they can have a soft light to help them find their way without disturbing anyone else.

Don’t have a home security system? You don’t need one: Devices like this $50 Philips Hue motion sensor work independently and can automatically tell smart lights what to do when someone approaches.

For more on protecting and utilizing your smart home, take a look at our favorite DIY home security systems, our list of the best smart home devices and our total smart home cheat sheet for all platforms.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
  • Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.
  • According to recent reports, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

According to recent reports, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

Industry observers note that if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The firm already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Industry observers note that abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro proposal, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent people may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

Industry observers note that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The latest landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

According to recent reports, “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Industry observers note that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

“You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets owners view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

Sources indicate that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about newly introduced signings.

In a recent development, “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he noted.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he remarked.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I loved journaling as a child.
  • I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
  • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

According to recent reports, it all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

Industry observers note that after a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

Getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one major image using multiple sheets.

Industry observers note that since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

According to recent reports, but I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

There are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty quickly.

Recent findings suggest that another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid says will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a substantial deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That noted, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.

Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. #50920. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2234 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2234 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
  • Recent findings suggest that microsoft Outlook?
  • Something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some complications. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

Something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these issues, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

Industry observers note that adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at cybersecurity company CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

“This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

One significant reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

It has been revealed that if it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

It has been revealed that artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a significant or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

At the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

Sources indicate that even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should update. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

Sources indicate that another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

In a recent development, when I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he stated, “it’s bad.”.

Sources indicate that as owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He notes he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. Fresh AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

“You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand stated.

Recent findings suggest that things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning last week.

In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers claims CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

“Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers mentioned.

Despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

“The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” said Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

Industry observers note that the good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

It has been revealed that it still might not be enough, and Substantial Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

In a recent development, and defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said this week at the Newly introduced York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

That’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

“There’s effectively this significant backlog of security issues in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” said Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity company focused on connected devices.

Sources indicate that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

“Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse stated.

In a recent development, wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of issues is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with vital, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to update so frequently these days.

“It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” remarked Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

According to recent reports, and patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s complications on Tuesday.

Things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents newly introduced problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing issue.

Industry observers note that in the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

Major Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

“I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” said Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy says.

That means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into new software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

The main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

“I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he noted. “It will hurt a bit.”.

Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more crucial than ever.

Industry observers note that “You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers stated. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

According to recent reports, but consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a company isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

Recent findings suggest that we don’t have to put up with it, Barlet claims. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

According to recent reports, there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the newly introduced Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

Industry observers note that one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Industry observers note that agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of upcoming tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

According to recent reports, along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

#50917. Latest Update: One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1114 w)
📖 Baca
