Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1012 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people latest tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.
  • Sources indicate that muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches.
  • Industry observers note that AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people latest tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

Sources indicate that muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches. Meta’s Muse AI agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

Industry observers note that AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

It has been revealed that that’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

According to recent reports, given Meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security challenges, it’s worth proceeding with caution. A few months ago, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

Despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

Industry observers note that muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

Industry observers note that within weeks of launch earlier this fall, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that Meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency upgrade to MacOS privacy controls.

More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse consumers, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

Muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report indicates that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta rolled out the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

Muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN company Surfshark stated it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

In a recent development, emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the substantial positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Industry observers note that signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the latest year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Sources indicate that emery noted: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

According to recent reports, “Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another vital player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

Recent findings suggest that england centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

Industry observers note that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Industry observers note that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

It has been revealed that it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Industry observers note that before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

In a recent development, it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

What will we learn from the “latest Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Sources indicate that unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

According to recent reports, I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

Recent findings suggest that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

According to recent reports, “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

It has been revealed that “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

  • All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current owners will lose access to both next year.

All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

In a recent development, the change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

According to recent reports, google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

Industry observers note that as part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

Google says that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give people the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

According to recent reports, on Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

It has been revealed that for most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the firm starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Google indicates Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and consumers will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Industry observers note that gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google revealed earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Owners in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, this is not your parents’ Google home page.
  • The new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm.
  • Sources indicate that the buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more owners to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of fresh features worldwide.

The new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

Sources indicate that the buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the fresh buttons when signed in to my Google account.

When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

Industry observers note that clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a new page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”.

The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

Another upcoming feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which shows your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:.

Stein noted the new sidebar will help customers go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a significant difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Sources indicate that google will use your AI searches — whether they are questions, tasks, uploaded files or image generation — to train its AI models, but you can tell Google you’re opting out. CNET has an overview of how to tell chatbots not to use your data. Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google declared several other latest AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion customers in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the organization’s “fastest growing product ever.”.

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The Newly introduced York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts mentioned they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Sources indicate that google noted search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

Recent findings suggest that google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

  • It has been revealed that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an notable one for the brand.
  • The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hyundai pulled back the cover on the fresh 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

It has been revealed that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an notable one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

An updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a newly introduced Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Industry observers note that sharing the stage in LA, the new nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

It has been revealed that inside, a latest cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

It has been revealed that pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is stated to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s fresh AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai indicates the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

“Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” said Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the fresh Elantra is anything but bland.

Recent findings suggest that the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent newly introduced SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

The sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

According to recent reports, hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Recent findings suggest that editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround blueprint.

Recent findings suggest that following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," noted Wright.

It has been revealed that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the manufacturer's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the manufacturer's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it confirms its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

It has been revealed that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active owners in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that netflix (NFLX -2.96%) has Michael Burry's attention.
  • It has been revealed that that's a long way down.
  • With the stock trading near $58 as of this writing, a price in the high $30s would cut about another third off the shares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:22PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

Industry observers note that netflix (NFLX -2.96%) has Michael Burry's attention. Just not at today's price.

It has been revealed that that's a long way down. Netflix shares closed at $58.46 on Thursday, Nov. 19, their lowest close since May 2024 (using split-adjusted prices, because Netflix did a 10-for-1 stock split in November 2025).

With the stock trading near $58 as of this writing, a price in the high $30s would cut about another third off the shares.

I don't think investors have to wait for that. At today's price, Netflix already looks cheap for a company whose profits are still climbing.

Michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

According to recent reports, burry has been circling Netflix for months. In July, he figured that Netflix at $67.75 per share traded at about 1.6 times its intrinsic value, which comes out to a value of roughly $42 a share by his math. He also stated then that the stock would have to drop to the low $50s to get closer to an ideal buying opportunity.

So, the high $30s isn't a random number. It would let him buy under his own estimate of what the manufacturer is worth.

Industry observers note that his concern is how long Netflix's content keeps its value. In July, he compared the streaming giant to Walt Disney and its Pixar studio, whose content he called evergreen. Much of what Netflix makes, he suggested, is OK for now but doesn't improve with age.

Sure, that's a fair worry about any business built on hit shows. But it's a long-term debate. In the meantime, Netflix's profits keep growing, making the high $30s look like a really pessimistic price.

Call the high $30s $38 a share. On average, analysts expect Netflix to earn about $3.80 per share in 2027, so a $38 stock would cost about 10 times next year's expected earnings. At around $58, shares trade at about 15 times next year's expected earnings.

Industry observers note that by comparison, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) traded at 17.7 times its expected earnings for the next 12 months on Nov. 5, according to FactSet.

Said another way, Netflix stock already costs less than the average stock relative to its earnings. Burry's price would put it at a discount of over 40% to the market's price-to-earnings ratio.

For $38 to be a market-average price, Netflix would have to earn only about $2.15 per share. It earned $2.53 per share in 2025 (split-adjusted too), and its earnings per share have grown year over year in every quarter of 2026 so far.

The high $30s would only make sense, then, if Netflix's profits were about to shrink.

In a recent development, they don't look close to shrinking. Netflix's operating margin was 26.7% in 2024 and 29.5% in 2025, and the business is targeting 31.5% for 2026. Its third-quarter operating margin hit 34.6%. And management is guiding for a 26% margin in the fourth quarter, above the 24.5% Netflix reported a year before, even with costs from newly unveiled job cuts. All told, Netflix notes its outlook implies operating income growth of over 20% this year.

Also, Netflix keeps returning cash to shareholders. It spent $4.8 billion buying back its own stock in the third quarter alone, and it still had $22.3 billion in repurchase authorizations left.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that sales growth, though, keeps slowing. Revenue growth has fallen every quarter this year, to 11.8% year over year in the third quarter from 16.2% in the first. And management expects around 11.5% for the fourth quarter, while it has lowered its 2026 ad revenue outlook to about $2.7 billion from about $3 billion.

But a business still growing sales by double digits while raising its operating margin looks unlikely to wind up earning less than it did in 2025.

Could Burry still get his price? He might. Netflix stock is already down over half from its June 2025 record, and a stock that's fallen this far can keep falling.

In a recent development, but waiting for the high $30s is arguably a bet that Netflix's earnings stall. At around 15 times next year's expected earnings, Netflix stock already prices in a lot of caution, I think. I'd consider buying shares now rather than waiting for Burry's number.

#50880. I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1656 w)

I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
  • According to recent reports, take Southwest Airlines, for example.
  • In a recent development, "Experiences create lifetime memories,” claims Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

According to recent reports, take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

In a recent development, "Experiences create lifetime memories,” claims Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

In a recent development, southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but massive-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

Industry observers note that even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

It has been revealed that as of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

$1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

According to recent reports, four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

If you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

Industry observers note that using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

Industry observers note that daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

It has been revealed that ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

Sources indicate that again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

Sources indicate that grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

According to recent reports, with that mentioned, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

Recent findings suggest that scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

Industry observers note that finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

Industry observers note that personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” claims Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Realty Income has an excellent track record, a high yield, and plenty of reasons to be confident about its future success. If you invest $10,000 right now, here's how much you can expect to get in dividends in 2027.

Realty Income has supported its top dividend by running a massive real estate business that leases properties to large essential retailers. These are chains you know and love and likely shop at, like Walmart (WMT +1.51%), Home Depot (HD +0.70%), 7-Eleven, and Dollar General (DG -2.23%).

These are stores with well-established brands and strong cash flow, making them reliable renters. They have multi-year leases, some as long as 20 years, and Realty Income's occupancy rate is a high 98.8%. It has maintained a rate between 97% and 99% since 2000.

Grocery and convenience stores make up almost 20% of the portfolio, providing a resilient revenue stream, but the company has also branched out into other areas as it expands and diversifies. The U.K. is one of its largest markets today, accounting for more than 15% of total properties, and Wynn Resorts (WYNN -2.07%) has become one of its biggest customers. Industrials make up a healthy 17% of the portfolio, and Realty Income is also getting started in data centers, which make up 1%.

The company has more than 15,500 properties in 96 industries, and it's always buying latest properties to keep growing. It has a $5.5 billion revolving credit facility, and it's raised more than $2 billion so far this year from various sources. It has a large pipeline of quality properties to choose from, and expanding beyond retail offers it more opportunities.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Realty Income has paid a dividend monthly for the past 677 months, or more than 56 years. It's one of the few dividend stocks that cuts you a check every month.

Industry observers note that it also raises its dividend quarterly rather than annually, which is unusual among great dividend stocks. It has raised the dividend for the past 117 quarters, or more than 29 years.

At the current price, the dividend yields 5.6%, an excellent yield for a reliable dividend stock.

Sources indicate that realty Income is a dividend play, and the stock hasn't changed much over the past 10 years. However, now has been a particularly challenging time for the firm as interest and mortgage rates remain high.

Since its business model involves borrowing lots of money, higher interest rates mean it has to pay more to service its debt.

While shares are down 7% over the last six months, it doesn’t appear to be in any danger, and it’s flourished across a range of environments for more than 50 years, paying its dividend without missing a monthly payment.

As of its latest raise last week, Realty Income pays $3.288 in annualized dividends, up from $3.258. That's a small change of only 0.9%. If it continues like that for the next four quarters, by the end of 2027, it should be $3.408 in annualized dividends. The average of the two is $3.348, and divided by 12, that's an average monthly payment of $0.279.

If you invest $10,000 today at a share price of $57.66 (at the time of writing), that gets you 173 shares, and next year, you'd get about $48.27 every month.

  • Sources indicate that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you look up at the sky tonight, you'll notice the Moon is looking noticeably fuller than it did earlier in the week. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase, which falls between the First Quarter and Full Moon, but we're getting closer to the Full Moon every night.

According to recent reports, as of Saturday, Nov. 21, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 85% of its surface visible.

Sources indicate that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Frigoris, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 15 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Hyginus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Latest Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

Sources indicate that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Industry observers note that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 6:40PM EST.
  • Investors often find themselves choosing between specialized software leaders and broad infrastructure giants.
  • Intuit serves as the backbone for personal and small business finances, while Oracle provides the essential databases and cloud infrastructure that large organizations require.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 6:40PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Intuit ›.

Investors often find themselves choosing between specialized software leaders and broad infrastructure giants. Deciding whether to buy Intuit (INTU -12.77%) or Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) depends on your preference for consumer stability versus enterprise growth.

Intuit serves as the backbone for personal and small business finances, while Oracle provides the essential databases and cloud infrastructure that large organizations require. Both companies are right now integrating artificial intelligence to enhance their platforms. This comparison examines their growth rates, balance sheets, and relative valuations to determine which stock fits best in a 2027 outlook.

Recent findings suggest that intuit provides essential financial technology solutions for millions of global consumers and small businesses through its core brands like TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Credit Karma. The organization presently serves approximately 93 million owners and relies on major distribution platforms like the Apple (AAPL -1.90%) App Store and Google Play Store. To support its vast software ecosystem, it maintains strategic partnerships with major cloud infrastructure providers including Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) and Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (NASDAQ:GOOG).

In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $21.9 billion, representing growth of close to 12.8% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for this time frame was approximately $4.8 billion, reflecting the organization's ability to maintain high net margins while expanding its user base. This steady financial expansion is largely driven by consistent, recurring demand for its digital accounting and tax preparation platforms among mid-market businesses.

Recent findings suggest that as of its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is nearly 0.4x, a metric that compares total debt against the value of shareholder equity to assess financial leverage. The current ratio is approximately 1.5x, reflecting a healthy ability to pay short-term obligations using its most liquid assets. In the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $8.7 billion, though note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Oracle offers enterprise software, cloud applications, and infrastructure services through a global delivery model that serves corporations, government agencies, and educational institutions. The company distributes its complex database systems and cloud applications in more than 145 countries and operates through a network of resellers and system integrators. It recently focused on expanding its presence in tech stocks by building out massive data center capacity specifically designed for high-performance artificial intelligence workloads.

It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Aug. 31, 2026, revenue reached close to $71.8 billion, a significant growth rate of approximately 21.6%. Net income for this period was nearly $18.9 billion, showcasing the scale of its operations as it transitions legacy customers to its newer cloud models. This robust increase in sales is largely attributed to the rapid adoption of its cloud infrastructure services and the ongoing modernization of enterprise data systems.

Recent findings suggest that as of its May 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 3.7x, indicating that the company uses a substantial amount of debt relative to its equity to fund its capital-intensive operations. The current ratio is roughly 1.1x, suggesting that its ability to meet immediate financial obligations is at the moment lean compared to more liquid software rivals. In the fiscal year ended May 31, 2026, free cash flow was a negative $23.7 billion because its massive investments in data center equipment and physical assets exceeded the cash generated from day-to-day operations.

Intuit faces intense competition from established rivals and start-ups in the financial software space, particularly those offering lower-cost tax preparation alternatives. The business is heavily dependent on the highly seasonal U.S. tax filing period, which creates significant fluctuations in its annual results and can amplify the impact of any operational delays. It also faces ongoing risks from cybersecurity threats and complex regulatory oversight regarding data privacy and the implementation of artificial intelligence within its consumer products.

Oracle contends with fierce competition in the cloud and software industry from giants like Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Amazon. The tech giant deals with a complex supply chain and potential volatility from international operations, including geopolitical instability and trade restrictions that could affect global deployments. Its large-scale transition to a cloud-first strategy requires consistent execution and significant capital spending to avoid losing market share to more specialized infrastructure providers.

With a slightly lower Forward P/E relative to future earnings estimates and a more attractive P/S ratio, Intuit right now trades at a valuation discount relative to Oracle.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with Intuit. Small businesses build their books, payroll, and payments around its software, which makes it hard to leave and gives Intuit a dependable base to grow from. And it is now beginning to win larger companies. QuickBooks, TurboTax, and Credit Karma are brands many people already know, and its software for mid-sized businesses is growing about 40% year over year.

It has been revealed that what I like is that Intuit keeps returning cash to shareholders, with a dividend that rose 15% over the past year, and it is building AI into its products, so customers can now use QuickBooks inside AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. Its latest quarter also came in above the tech giant's own targets, and it expects solid growth this year.

To give Oracle its due, it rents out the computing power AI companies need, and its cloud infrastructure sales have more than doubled year over year. But it is borrowing heavily to build data centers and burning cash while it does, and a big share of its contracts comes from one customer, OpenAI.

Intuit's growth, by contrast, comes with healthy profits and cash returned to shareholders, not a heavy debt load. For long-term investors, a profitable software company that is expanding into bigger businesses makes Intuit the better buy for 2027.

An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
  • According to recent reports, if you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
  • Sources indicate that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The massive day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

According to recent reports, if you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

Sources indicate that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, indicates Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

According to recent reports, non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

According to recent reports, neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold claims.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

“Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” indicates Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley notes.

According to recent reports, got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

“Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

According to recent reports, electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

Gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath claims. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

That noted, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold claims.

It has been revealed that for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, notes consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

“Significant-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

According to recent reports, many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Sources indicate that shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold says. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath notes. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch notes. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch indicates.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch says. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

Check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

Recent findings suggest that use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The resignation of Jensen Huang sent shockwaves through the investment world, with the longtime CEO of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stepping down following allegations of multiple affairs, including with subordinates and a potential Chinese spy.
  • Let's look at three things that could go right for the semiconductor stock without Huang, and three things that can go wrong.
  • In a recent development, the biggest thing that could go right with Huang gone is that Nvidia's moat remains intact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:41PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

The resignation of Jensen Huang sent shockwaves through the investment world, with the longtime CEO of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stepping down following allegations of multiple affairs, including with subordinates and a potential Chinese spy. With its co-founder no longer at its helm, some things will certainly change for the tech giant.

Let's look at three things that could go right for the semiconductor stock without Huang, and three things that can go wrong.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, the biggest thing that could go right with Huang gone is that Nvidia's moat remains intact. The tech giant's moat has long been its CUDA operating system, on which most original artificial intelligence (AI) code was written and optimized for its graphics processing units (GPUs). However, with AI models now showing they can help run models on other chips in just a few days, this moat is rapidly shrinking.

It has been revealed that CUDA is not Nvidia's only edge, though, and right now it has a large supply chain moat. It has locked down a lot of future supply-constrained high-bandwidth memory (HBM) through a $500 billion deal with SK Hynix (SKHY -13.11%), and it also has the most access to fab capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -9.48%). In a supply-constrained market, availability matters, and right now this is one of Nvidia's biggest advantages.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

Nvidia is growing promptly, and that is expected to continue, with the company recently forecasting that its revenue would climb 75% in fiscal 2028. This growth is being led not just by surging GPU demand, but also by the company getting an ever-increasing piece of the data center revenue pie.

With its Hopper architecture, Nvidia was capturing about $18 billion in revenue per gigawatt of capacity. Through networking, the addition of more chips like central processing units (CPUs) and language processing units (LPUs), and a more robust software stack, Nvidia is now getting $40 billion per gigawatt for its Vera Rubin System. Keep expanding its system to capture more revenue opportunities, and Nvidia's strong growth will continue.

Trading at a forward P/E of only 9 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates, Nvidia's stock is cheap and has the potential for some substantial multiple expansion. The company will just have to show that it can continue to grow under latest leadership.

Under Huang, Nvidia developed a close relationship with Elon Musk and SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%), which decided to exclusively build out its data centers on Vera Rubin. SpaceX is set to be one of the most aggressive companies in the space, and if the loss of Huang changes this relationship, it could be a blow to Nvidia's future growth.

Musk has already said he wants Huang to join his tech giant, and if he does and the company pursues its own chips, it would be a blow to Nvidia.

According to recent reports, even before Huang's departure, there was a push to slow the data center build-out in the U.S., with a large contingent of anti-data-center candidates winning key seats in the midterm elections. This is most likely to impact neoclouds, a major source of revenue for Nvidia.

Sources indicate that any delays not only reduce potential sales, but could trigger financing issues for these customers. Neoclouds and enterprise made up 44% of Nvidia's data center revenue in fiscal Q3, so this is no small matter.

In a recent development, perhaps the biggest risk Nvidia faces with Huang gone is the potential for lost market share and margin compression. Custom AI accelerators and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) have been gaining share, and Nvidia's CUDA moat now appears to be dwindling.

Industry observers note that if this causes the company to slash prices to stay competitive, it would significantly reduce its gross margins, potentially putting pressure on earnings even if sales were to continue to grow. This would likely cause the stock to tumble.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

Industry observers note that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Industry observers note that on Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

Recent findings suggest that the results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you blueprint to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

Sources indicate that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

Recent findings suggest that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

Industry observers note that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

Latest Update: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

💡 Key Takeaways
